title: Cebu metal box
description: These metal box are more common in the southern half of the island.

title: Davao Oriental support pole setup
description: This specific setup of electric meter are quite common north of the Davao Oriental region

title: Western Davao meters setup
description: This setup with the meter attached to a simple rectangle metal support are found in Davao Oriental.

title: Hook meter setup
description: When the tube going from the bottom of the metter to the top with this "hook" like shape. You are around General Santos City

title: Benguet Province metal box
description: Metal box with slatted windows are found in the benguet state.

title: Ilocos Sur blue metal box
description: This version of the box with two rows of circle windows are found in Ilocos sur. They must be painted in blue! If not you are in La Union

title: La Union metal box
description: Same as Ilocos Sur metal box but these boxes are not painted blue.

title: Bataan grey cover
description: One meta for the province of Bataan is this specific type of grey cover for the counters. The cover seems to be specifically designed for this style of counter and is unique to Bataan.

title: Batan counter
description: This type of counter itself can be recognized by the location of the screen and the circle with two dots in it. This counter is most common in Bataan within Luzon, it occasionally appears elsewhere, for example in Eastern Samar.

title: Occidental Mindoro electric counters
description: For whatever reason, across all of Occidental Mindoro, electricity counters are commonly attached to what appears to be cutting boards. Very common and consistent meta.

title: Aklan meters board
description: The most useful meta for the province of Aklan is the yellow metal sheet that the electricity counters are attached to. Occasionally Aklan will also use wooden planks.

title: Antique meters board
description: Antique will feature a yellow metal cover similar to what’s found in Aklan but it will also feature a roof. In the far north, Antique will also sometimes use wooden planks.

title: Capiz counter board
description: Capiz features a yellow cover similar to what can be found in Antique. This cover can be distinguished using the tab on top of the roof as well as the triangular walls found on either end.

title: Northern Iloilo counter box
description: The Northern half of Iloilo will feature this yellow metal cover that features a handle design.

title: Southern Iloilo meter board
description: The Southern half of Iloilo features the same yellow metal covers that can be found in Antique.

title: Guimaras counters
description: Guimaras features many of the same yellow covers that can be found across Antique and Iloilo. One way to distinguish the island is by using this specific counter pictured. While it won’t always appear, when it does it seems to be fairly unique within Panay.

title: Samar counter
description: A flat grey plastic cover can be found in the bottom half of Samar. It’s common for the front panel to be missing.

title: Negros Occidental electric counters
description: These tall thin slats of metal they use to mount the counters to, seems to be found in the bottom 80% of Negros Occidental.This is also rarely found in Northern Luzon and smaller variants can be found in Mindanao

title: Zamboanga del Norte pink board
description: In this region it isn’t that uncommon to find counters that are attached to a pink board

title: Zamboanga del Sur counters
description: The northern part of Zamboanga del Sur loves to use these square and rectangular counters. They will often be attached to metal strips that resemble a ribcage.

title: Sultan Kudarat
description: One unique cover found commonly in Sultan Kudarat is the metal box with circles carved out in every corner.

title: Island of Samal electric counters
description: On the island of Samal it’s quite common for the tubes to be wrapped in lots of black tape.

title: Zamboanga Peninsula trike
description: Airplane-shaped passenger window, roof leaning back, trike bulging out from under the window. Singular window in the back. The only variant seen on the entire Zamboanga Peninsula.

title: Dipolog City trike variantm
description: Tiny window over the driver's side and a big number on the roof. Variant of the Zamboanga Peninsula trike.

title: Ozamiz City trike
description: Bubbly numbers on top of the driver's window (any color scheme). Exclusive to Ozamiz City and surrounding areas.

title: Zamboanga City trike
description: Flat roof, white line separating passenger and driver's side, bumper under the window. Super colorful trikes. Identifiable from behind by black cloth roof, large window with white line, and back side window.

title: Zamboanga City trike variantm
description: These less colorful variants can be found Northeast of the main city.

title: Umbrella trikes
description: Trikes with an umbrella instead of a roof. Super common in Maguindanao, Misamis Occidental, and Lanao del Sur. Really the only trikes in Cotabato city. Also very common in Cebu.

title: Maguindanao square roof trikes
description: Trikes with a square roof, very common within Maguindanao.

title: Sultan Kudarat trike
description: Large flat black roof, small side window, no lines in the main window. Green trikes with blue POBLACION text are specific to Isulan. Colorful variant with number on top specific to Tacurong City.

title: Koronadal trike
description: Lower passenger car with a crown above the window and a curvy bit underneath. Downtown Koronadal ones are all yellow. Same shape in different colors found throughout the area.

title: Koronadal trike variant
description: This variant with a bar underneath the passenger

title: General Santos trike
description: Window extends out at an angle, roof leans forward, 2 or 3 lines on the window, two baby windows underneath. This specific shade of blue is found in downtown General Santos.

title: Polomolok trike
description: Orange variant of the General Santos trike shape, exclusive to Polomolok (slightly north of General Santos).

title: Cotabato trike
description: Crown on top, one or two windows leaning forward, underneath the windows the trike leans back. Flat roof also leans back. Kidapawan uses an exclusively white version.

title: Kidapawan Trike
description: The city of Kidapawan uses an exclusively white version of the Cotabato trike

title: Bukidnon trike
description: Very long trike with a main square window and two side windows (trifold pattern). Leaning backwards, usually has a crown on top. Side windows on the back.

title: Cagayan de Oro / Iligan metal outline trike
description: Metal outline of a trike shape, good clue for Cagayan de Oro and Iligan City.

title: Cagayan de Oro trike
description: A more fun Cagayan de Oro trike is this really colorful guy with a number on top, a big metal bar, and two tiny side windows. It looks like a mini-bus. It’s harder to identify from behind tho so gl with that.

title: Tagum lime green trike
description: Car-looking trikes in lime green, specific to Tagum. Common throughout Eastern Mindanao in other colors.

title: Downtown Surigao trike
description: Super long window with 2 or 3 lines, bumper under the window, back bar with side window. Can be any color.

title: East Mindanao standard trike
description: Two side windows plus a bottom window, main windows more equally shaped with a handlebar. Bottom windows are very ovular.

title: Mati trike
description: Crown, main window leaning back, bumper underneath with a little mini window on the bumper. Mati exclusive.

title: Southern Davao del Norte trike
description: Flat roof, flat window, has a crown and a bunch of windows in the back.

title: Davao City trike
description: Two big windows, bar underneath, big flat roof, windows leaning back. Can have a crown. Thing sticking out from bottom more common in downtown Davao.

title: Digos City yellow trike
description: Yellow variant of the Davao City trike shape, with two little windows on the back. Exclusive to Digos City.

title: Other trikes that exist in Mindanao
description: Other trikes that exist in Mindanao

title: bigass passenger window trike
description: These trikes I aptly labeled as the ‘bigass passenger window trike’ because they have a bigass passenger window. They also have a bunch of random bars- one handlebar near the passenger window and another one below it, and also there’s a window above the driver. The variant on the right that has a window below the passenger also exists.

title: L shape trike
description: This is the tetris L shape trike (stands what you’re gonna take vs me in geoguessr lol!!) that’s pretty localized to downtown Kalilangan.

title: Cotabato alternate trike
description: Cotabato alternate trike: it has a lot of these cool bar things on the passenger window, and the driver’s side has this really big window along with two tiny side windows (tiny trifold.) The driver can also sometimes have a big rectangle plank behind them.

title: Standard Leyte trike
description: Two windows slightly tilting away from each other, huge curved crown at the top, roof leaning back. Trikes much more common in Leyte than Mindanao, even on rural highways.

title: Tacloban City red trike
description: Red trikes with numbers on the bottom, can have 1 or 2 windows, roofs can be any color.

title: Ormoc City green trike
description: Green ones with combined window, bar underneath leaning outwards and another bar underneath leaning backwards. Common in Ormoc City, western Leyte.

title: Leyte bikes
description: These regular bikes with a small cart attached to them are super common throughout Leyte as well. There’s also another variant with intricate metal around it and a roof on top are also super common throughout the island & Samar (beware that these can occasionally be found outside of Eastern Visayas though)

title: Western Leyte uneven roof trike
description: Uneven roof trike with two large 'iPad' sized windows and a very long vertical bit underneath the passenger side.

title: Eastern Leyte connecting window trike
description: Variant with a connecting window and two crowns above the windows, more common on the eastern part of Leyte.

title: trikes that have multiple benches
description: These trikes that have multiple benches and are kind of tuktuk shaped are found sporadically in specific cities in Leyte. Specifically, San Isidro, Isabela, and Hilongos use these.

title: Samar trike
description: Similar to Leyte trikes but with a flat roof leaning back less, a little car thing at the bottom. Tend to be fatter. Black roofs more common than in Leyte.

title: Southern Samar Trek
description: Southern Samar has these uneven windows, and Samar also uses black roofs more often than Leyte.

title: Western Samar trike
description: Really small in size, two large windows and a connecting window, very low passenger trike. Specific shade of red common in Catbalogan City. Singular window in the back.

title: Masbate trike
description: Driver's side completely open with a roof covering, passenger side has a large window, crown, bars, and hexagon shape. Yellow = Masbate City, yellow with silver accents = Cataingan.

title: Masbate trike
description: There’s also this quirky open variant that’s found in some parts of the island, but it has the same shape as the rest.

title: Bohol trike
description: Large and boxy with one large window, a crown, and a distinctive little window below the larger one. Often black roofs. Tagbilaran City has unique back with 4 windows.

title: Tagbilaran trikes
description: Tagbilaran trikes will have this unique back with 4 windows. This is exclusive to the city. Also, a lot of bohol trikes will have black roofs.

title: Bohol tuk tuk
description: These tuktuk looking trikes are exclusive to Bohol as well. What separates them is their lil horns hanging from the front as mirrors, and the small side windows. They look pretty generic from the back, but have two back windows.

title: NE Cebu R2D2 trike
description: Flat roof, robot-looking sidecar, very rectangular prism shaped, back like a pickup truck. Found in northeast Cebu.

title: Northern Cebu NEOOR trike
description:
Racecar-looking passenger seat, driver's roof leans forward, sticky outy thing at bottom, solid colors. Very blocky from behind with small back window.
Category: car

title: Western Cebu
description: compilation of all the ones I mapped.

title: Southern Cebu long window trike
description: Iconic long window trikes, can be double or single windowed. Most common in southern Cebu.

title: umbrella trikes
description: the umbrella trikes can be found everywhere throughout the island as well.

title: Dumaguete trike
description: Thinner metal, numbered at the bottom. Northern variant is larger with a thingy sticking out under the passenger side and two side windows.

title: Northern Negros NEOOR trike
description: NEOOR trike with a larger passenger window compared to the Cebu variant, slightly different shape. The second picture : These guys with a square roof are found more South in the island (near Kabankalan.)

title: other trikes that exist in Negros
description: some other trikes that exist in Negros

title: Guimaras trike
description: Very open at the sides, random window bits, racecar/Zamboanga coded, tall passenger window.

title: Narra trike (South Palawan)
description: Car-shaped, mint colored, very wide, seen sporadically throughout south Palawan.

title: Northern Palawan trike
description: Very wide with big front windows. Black bit on top doesn't take up as much space (balding look).

title: Southern Panay trike
description: NEOOR coded but leans back much farther, no sticky outy bits on passenger window. Standard Iloilo City shape.

title: Western Panay trike
description: Western Panay loves this mini window over the passenger.

title: more shapes trikes in Panay
description: Here are some more shapes that can be found in Panay.

title: more shapes in Panay 2
description: Here are some more shapes that can be found in Panay.

title: Mindoro trike
description: Curvy side bars around driver's side, curved mattress on top of driver with a cap underneath, metal trifold windows around passenger. Very common throughout Mindoro.

title: Western Mindoro variant
description: Koronadal-adjacent trikes where the bottom juts out more rather than the top. Metal outlines around driver's side.

title: andom Mindoro variant
description: This is another random Mindoro variant- note the curved mattress above the driver, the bar, and the cap above the driver. Also Mindoro uses a lot of aluminum/silver colored trikes.

title: Standard Bicol trike
description: Lots of windows for both driver and passenger, big connecting window, lots of side and back windows. Open driver's side.

title: Bicol trike
description: This is still identifiable as a Bicol trike due to the open driver’s side and the billion windows.

title: middle Bicol variant
description: This is the middle Bicol variant with a small mini window underneath the driver’s side. It appears to be found most commonly North of Legazpi city.

title: middle Bicol variant
description: This is the middle Bicol variant with a small mini window underneath the driver’s side. It appears to be found most commonly North of Legazpi city.

title: Ligao / Sorsogon city-specific trikes
description: Ligao likes silver trikes, Sorsogon City uses yellow ones.

title: Daet silver trike
description: Aluminum silver trikes in huge numbers, slightly short with a crown that looks slightly too large. Exclusive to Daet.

title: Daet tuk tuk variant
description: Daet tuk tuk but not grey

title: Standard Calabarzon trike
description: Mattresses above both passenger and driver, curvy bar in front of driver, distinctive shape with belt underneath window. Tiny back window. Found throughout Calabarzon.

title: Middle Calabarzon trike
description: Only mildly regional one is this variant with a connecting window.

title: Calabarzon trike
description: These types of trikes are identifiable from behind due to the tiny back window and the cart shape as well- here’s the Calabarzon trike distribution (it’s in Calabarzon.)

title: Manila trike
description: Manila trike rapidfire- idk just look at the mattress above the driver and the shape of the passenger car. There’s a lot of random variety & some parts seem to be more color coded but I can’t be bothered to research Manila regionguessing

title: Calabarzon Plates
description: Calabarzon shape extends all throughout Central Luzon, but they lack the Calabarzon bar on the driver’s side. Cabanatuan City also tends to have these license plates on the front of their trikes. Some Central Luzon trikes have crowns on them as well.

title: Central Luzon trike
description: Same Calabarzon shape but lacks the bar on the driver's side. Cabanatuan City tends to have license plates on the front. Some have crowns.

title: Bataan double window trike
description: Double windowed trikes very concentrated within Bataan. Can also have normal trikes with metallic outside.

title: Western luzon trike
description: Western luzon along the coast has this variant with a metal trifold around the passenger + a crown.

title: Pangasinan / Ilocos crown trike
description: Trikes with crowns on them, found in Pangasinan province and along the Luzon coast up to Vigan city (La Union, Ilocos Sur).

title: Candon City yellow trike
description: All yellow trikes with numbers at the top, exclusive to Candon City.

title: Cagayan Valley trike
description: Trifold window with characteristic black back covering. Window above driver, tons of windows. Bambang variant has 20 billion stickers.

title: variant Cagayan Valley trike
description: This variant with the connecting window between the driver and the passenger is more common more North of the province.

title: Cagayan Valley variant
description: Another Cagayan Valley trike is this guy with the metal trifold around the driver’s window, sometimes it comes with two crowns as well. This one is found more North of Tuguegarao.

title: Northern Luzon tiny sidecar trike
description: Very boxy trike with a tiny sidecar, open passenger windows, and a square-ish window.
